dossier.public_summary: TESS shows a ~1.5-ppt, ~2-hour dip every 6.2 days that difference imaging places on the target M dwarf with no nearby star able to mimic it. The dip is flat-bottomed with no odd/even or secondary eclipses and implies a 3 Earth-radius planet, consistent with a high-impact transit. The detection is real, though the star is spotted and makes follow-up mass measurement the key remaining test.

reasons.why: Difference image puts the dip on the target; closest neighbours that could cause it are >111 arcsec away.
